frontText:
Move one character left. Which key?

```
cat
 ●
←┘
```
backText:
```
h
```

Left in the `h j k l` cluster. Hold it to keep moving.

[Left-right motions](https://vimhelp.org/motion.txt.html#left-right-motions)

frontText:
Move down one line. Which key?

```
one
 ●
 ↓
two
```
backText:
```
j
```

Down. Hold `j` to repeat the movement.

[Up-down motions](https://vimhelp.org/motion.txt.html#up-down-motions)

frontText:
Move up one line. Which key?

```
one
 ↑
 ●
two
```
backText:
```
k
```

Up. Hold `k` to repeat the movement.

[Up-down motions](https://vimhelp.org/motion.txt.html#up-down-motions)

frontText:
Move one character right. Which key?

```
cat
 ●
 └→
```
backText:
```
l
```

Right in the `h j k l` cluster. Hold it to keep moving.

[Left-right motions](https://vimhelp.org/motion.txt.html#left-right-motions)

frontText:
Jump to the next word start. Which key?

```
const userName
●─────→
```
backText:
```
w
```

Jumps to the start of the next word. Takes a count: `3w` jumps three words.

[Word motions](https://vimhelp.org/motion.txt.html#word-motions)

frontText:
Jump to the previous word start. Which key?

```
const userName
←─────●
```
backText:
```
b
```

Jumps to the start of the previous word — the backward counterpart of `w`.

[Word motions](https://vimhelp.org/motion.txt.html#word-motions)

frontText:
Jump straight to the first line.

```
1    ← target
│
●    line 500
│
EOF
```
backText:
```
gg
```

`1gg` and `1G` also go to line 1.

[Up-down motions](https://vimhelp.org/motion.txt.html#up-down-motions)

frontText:
Jump straight to the last line.

```
1    ●
│
│
EOF  ← target
```
backText:
```
G
```

`$G` also reaches the last line, but `G` is shorter.

[Up-down motions](https://vimhelp.org/motion.txt.html#up-down-motions)

```
Ctrl-f
```

Hold Ctrl and press `f`: forward, like Page Down.

[Scrolling](https://vimhelp.org/scroll.txt.html)

```
Ctrl-b
```

Hold Ctrl and press `b`: backward, like Page Up.

[Scrolling](https://vimhelp.org/scroll.txt.html)

frontText:
Jump to the next whitespace-separated **WORD**, skipping the punctuation inside `foo.bar`.

```
foo.bar   baz
●─────────→
```
backText:
```
W
```

`W` treats everything between spaces as one WORD; `w` stops at punctuation.

[WORD motions](https://vimhelp.org/motion.txt.html#WORD)

frontText:
Jump back to the previous whitespace-separated **WORD**.

```
foo.bar   baz
←─────────●
```
backText:
```
B
```

`B` is the backward counterpart of `W`; `b` also stops at punctuation.

[WORD motions](https://vimhelp.org/motion.txt.html#WORD)

frontText:
Use Command-line mode to jump to line 32.

```
 31
→32  target
 33
```
backText:
```vim
:32<Enter>
```

An Ex line address jumps directly to that line.

[Ex command lines](https://vimhelp.org/cmdline.txt.html#cmdline-lines)

frontText:
Use Command-line mode to jump to the last line.

```
1
│
│
EOF  ← target
```
backText:
```vim
:$<Enter>
```

In an Ex line address, `$` means the last line.

[Ex command lines](https://vimhelp.org/cmdline.txt.html#cmdline-lines)

frontText:
Move down continuously using keyboard repeat.

```
● line 1
│
│
▼ line 4
```
backText:
```
hold j
```

Holding any `h`, `j`, `k`, or `l` key repeats that movement. For long jumps, prefer `gg` or `G`.

[Up-down motions](https://vimhelp.org/motion.txt.html#up-down-motions)
